The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.24% for the week of October 29th, per Freddie Mac. In January 2021 it hit 2.65%, the lowest in the survey's history back to 1971.

On a $400,000 loan, principal and interest go from $1,612 a month to $2,726. Over 30 years, total interest goes from about $180,000 to about $581,000.

Lenders charge more when they expect each dollar to buy less over the life of the loan. Savers feel it from the other side: a down payment saved in dollars has to keep up with prices.

Sources: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms and https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-hit-new-record-low-first-week-2021
